| :---- | ----- |
| Youth Survey (160 respondents): 15.2% (24) interested 5.49% (9) somewhat interested 79.31% (127) uninterested in agriculture  Possible shift: Innovation: 65.52% (105)  Food security: 82.76% (132) Negative perception baseline: “Hard/back-breaking”: 44.14% (71) “Old-fashioned”: 57.69% (92) “Low income”: 40.34% (65) “Dirty”: 35.45% (57) Strategic Insight: This tells a powerful story arc we will use: The problem is NOT a lack of interest The problem is a lack of SYSTEM \+ ACCESS \+ MODERNIZATION |  |
| Fruit Vendors/Farmers (10 respondents): Data Insights: 80% (8) are willing to adopt 20% (2) are not willing to adopt 70% (7) use paper tracking 30% (3) rely purely on memory High spoilage risk during hot seasons (banana, papaya, mango) Price volatility due to oversupply from Bukidnon Key Insight: They lose money not due to lack of effort, but lack of timing and price awareness Quotable Feedback: “If it alerts me before my fruits spoil and shows market prices, I won’t be forced to sell too cheap.” |  |
| Vegetable Vendors / Farmers (10 respondents) Data Insights: 90% (9) are willing to adopt 10% (1) is not willing to adopt Manual profit tracking (cost vs sales) Suffer from: Wilting (weight loss) Transport cost inefficiencies No automated net income computation Key Insight: Profit exists—but is invisible due to a lack of tracking systems Quotable Feedback: “If it calculates my real profit automatically, I will finally know if I am earning or just working.” |  |
| City Agriculturists (10 respondents) Data Insights: 100% (10) willing to adopt Data collection is: Fragmented Delayed Often missing No real-time visibility across barangays Key Insight: Government systems are data-poor, not resource-poor Quotable Feedback: “If farmers input data into one system, we can finally see real-time production across the city.” |  |
| Agriculture Students (10 respondents) Data Insights: 90% (9) are willing to adopt 10% (1) is not willing to adopt Major gap: Modern tech in school Manual farming in reality Risk of disengagement due to outdated systems Key Insight: The next generation is ready—but the system isn’t Quotable Feedback: “We are taught modern tools, but in the field everything is manual—this is why many don’t pursue farming.” |  |
| Smallholder Farmers (30 respondents) Data Insights: 80% (24) are willing to adopt 20% (6) are not willing to adopt 85% (26) rely on memory or middlemen No visibility on: Real income Market price Highly vulnerable to: Weather shocks Input cost spikes Key Insight: Farmers are operating “blind” in their own business Quotable Feedback: “I don’t even know if I am earning — I only know when the middleman pays me.” |  |
| Young Farmers (10 respondents) Data Insights: 90% (9) are willing to adopt 10% (1) is willing to adopt Already using: Excel Notes apps Face: Resistance from the older generation Limited financial credibility Key Insight: They need tools not just for farming, but for proving professionalism Quotable Feedback: “If I can show real financial data from our farm, I can finally get loans and scale.” |  |
| Agriculture Innovators (5 respondents) Data Insights: 100% (5) willing to adopt Already using: Advanced tools Hybrid digital systems Biggest barrier: Low tech literacy among grassroots farmers Key Insight: Innovation exists—but it doesn’t reach the masses Quotable Feedback: “Farmers don’t need more advice—they need a system that makes their work visible and measurable.” |  |
| **TOTAL VALIDATION SUMMARY (All 85 Respondents)** Total Yes: 72 respondents Total No: 13 respondents  Adoption Rate: 84.7% |  |

| **Slide 1: Title Page  KATH** | Isang makabata at makakalikasang araw po sa inyong lahat. We are Team Agriova, and we begin with a simple but urgent truth: If the hands that feed us disappear, who will feed the next generation? Today, we introduce Agriova: From Dirt to Digital—a mobile-first Farm ERP and integrated marketplace built to empower the next generation of Filipino farmers. |
|  |  |
| **Slide 2: Problem  KATH**&nbsp; | The Philippines is facing an agricultural crisis: data from PhilRice shows the average farmer is already 57 years old, while our own city-wide youth survey reveals that nearly 80% of youth reject farming as an outdated, low-income career. Our validation of 85 stakeholders under the supervision of the City Agriculture’s Office shows that 85% of smallholders currently operate blindly on manual guesswork—leaving them exploited by middlemen and locked out of bank loans due to a lack of financial data. Fortunately, the market is ready: that same 85% is eager to use a simple digital tool to track their data and scale&nbsp; |
|  |  |
| **Slide 3: Solution  GERLIE**&nbsp; | Agriova transforms agriculture from a fallback into a viable and modern career. We digitize farm operations through a mobile-first platform, helping farmers replace guesswork with real data. Through a built-in marketplace, farmers can sell directly to buyers and fellow businesses, reducing dependence on middlemen. At the same time, AI-assisted guidance provides simple, practical recommendations to support everyday decisions. All of this is designed for real farming conditions with low connectivity and simple user needs. |
|  |  |
| **Slide 4: Product  JCR** | Agriova is a mobile-first platform that combines farm management, AI guidance, and a marketplace into one system. Farmers can track their operations, receive simple recommendations, and directly sell their products—reducing reliance on middlemen and replacing guesswork with data. |
| **Slide 5: Target Market  GERLIE** | Our market is both large and validated from PSA data and RSBSA data from the CDO LGU. There are 9 to 10 million agricultural workers in the Philippines, with 4 to 5 million smallholder farmers as our core segment. From this, we target 500,000 to 1 million digitally capable farmers and agripreneurs, validated by both global insights and local field data. We begin with a focused pilot of 500 to 5,000 users across selected barangays. |
| **Slide 6: Revenue Model  JHEY** | Agriova operates on a scalable dual-engine revenue model centered on farmer success. The platform offers free basic access while earning a 5% commission from successful marketplace transactions between farmers and wholesale buyers. As users grow their operations, they can subscribe to premium features and enhanced AI recommendations for ₱169 per month. This approach removes high upfront costs and allows Agriova’s growth to scale alongside the success of its farmers.&nbsp; |
| **Slide 7: Competition  FRANCIS** | The market is split between complex enterprise systems and fragmented or manual solutions. Enterprise platforms like SAP and FarmERP are too expensive and technical for smallholder farmers, while single-feature apps and traditional systems like agri-vet stores and middlemen remain limited and disconnected. Agriova bridges this gap by offering a mobile-first, affordable, and fully integrated platform designed specifically for everyday farmers. |
| **Slide 8: Team  FRANCIS** | Our team is led by yours truly, supported by John Carl Ramirez and Jhey Gulde for development, Gerlie Campion for research, and Kathlen Grace Gultiano for UI/UX, combining technical expertise with real field insight. |
| **Slide 9: Summary  FRANCIS** | To summarize, Agriova addresses a critical national challenge—an aging agricultural workforce, a generation walking away from farming, and a system stuck in low-tech, low-income cycles. Our solution is a mobile-first, AI-assisted platform that transforms smallholder farmers into modern agripreneurs by giving them access to tools, data, and direct markets. By doing this, we improve income visibility, reduce dependence on middlemen, and make farming more accessible and sustainable. With validated demand exceeding 84%, we are now ready to scale, and we invite you to partner with Agriova to empower the next generation of digital agripreneurs.” |
